title: Is MYP Individuals and Societies Compulsory?
summary: Learn when MYP Individuals and Societies is compulsory, how Years 4-5 flexibility works, and what to check before choosing school subjects.
body_markdown:
The **MYP Individuals and Societies requirement** means that most students study this subject group throughout the Middle Years Programme. In MYP Years 1 to 3, schools normally provide all eight MYP subject groups. In Years 4 and 5, approved flexibility may reduce the programme to six groups, but **Individuals and Societies remains required** under that model.


This does not mean every student takes an identical course. A school may offer integrated humanities, history, geography, economics, or another course that satisfies the group’s requirements. School policy, local curriculum rules, and MYP certificate participation therefore affect the options on your subject-selection form.


### The MYP Individuals and Societies requirement


The[official IB MYP curriculum overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/) organizes the programme into eight subject groups:


- Language and literature
- Language acquisition
- Individuals and societies
- Sciences
- Mathematics
- Arts
- Physical and health education
- Design


Up to MYP Year 3, schools are expected to provide learning across all eight groups. The IB requires at least **50 teaching hours per year for each subject group** , although schools may allocate more.


In Years 4 and 5, schools may use **subject-group flexibility** to meet student needs or local educational requirements. Students then study at least six groups: language and literature, language acquisition or an approved alternative, individuals and societies, sciences, mathematics, and one subject from arts, design, or physical and health education.


MYP stage Status of Individuals and Societies


Years 1 to 3 Included among all eight subject groups


Years 4 and 5 without flexibility Continues as one of eight groups


Years 4 and 5 with flexibility Required within the six-group model


MYP certificate pathway Required as an assessed subject group


Flexibility does not allow students to drop any two subjects independently. The school decides whether to use it and must construct its options within IB rules. The[RevisionDojo guide to MYP subject choice](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/choice-of-subjects-how-schools-customize-myp-for-local-needs) explains why combinations differ between schools.


### Is it compulsory for the MYP certificate?


Yes. Students seeking the **IB MYP certificate** must complete an Individuals and Societies assessment within the required eAssessment combination. The IB’s[MYP passing criteria](https://ibo.org/about-the-ib/what-it-means-to-be-an-ib-student/recognizing-student-achievement/about-assessment/myp-passing-criteria/) also require language and literature, language acquisition or an accepted alternative, sciences, mathematics, and one subject from arts, design, or physical and health education.


Individuals and Societies is assessed through an on-screen examination for certificate candidates. Students also complete interdisciplinary assessment, the personal project, and their school’s service requirements. Full eAssessment is optional for schools, so not every MYP student pursues the certificate.


A student may consequently complete a school-based MYP education without entering the complete certificate assessment package. That distinction does not automatically remove the school’s responsibility to meet MYP subject-group requirements.


### What subject appears on the timetable?


**Individuals and Societies is a subject group, not one universal course title.** The[official Individuals and Societies overview](https://ibo.org/programmes/middle-years-programme/curriculum/individuals-and-societies/) allows schools to organize it through:


- **Discrete courses** , including history, geography, economics, politics, sociology, or philosophy
- **Modular courses** , covering several disciplines in sequence under one subject-group grade
- **Integrated courses** , often called humanities or social studies, combining multiple disciplines


One school might require integrated humanities, while another lets students choose between history and geography. Either arrangement can satisfy the same MYP requirement.


There is no universal topic list taught identically in every school. The[guide to MYP Individuals and Societies topics](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-topics-are-covered-in-myp-individuals-and-societies) shows how units may cover migration, conflict, trade, political systems, environmental change, urban development, or human rights.


### What can students choose?


Your **MYP Individuals and Societies subject choice** may concern the course within the group, not whether you study the group. Before submitting choices, ask your coordinator:


1. Which courses satisfy the Individuals and Societies requirement?
2. Does the school use flexibility in Years 4 and 5?
3. Am I registered for the full MYP certificate?
4. Do national curriculum rules affect my options?
5. Does later study require a particular course?
6. Can students change after teaching begins?


Do not rely only on course titles. Social studies, global studies, humanities, or world history may be the school’s official Individuals and Societies offering.


If several courses are available, compare their content and methods rather than looking for the easiest option. Consider whether you prefer historical sources, maps, statistics, economic models, political issues, or mixed case studies. Also examine how each course develops research, source evaluation, argument, and data interpretation.


The[RevisionDojo assessment guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/how-myp-individuals-and-societies-is-assessed) explains the group’s criteria-based expectations. Future plans can inform your choice, but Diploma Programme prerequisites are determined by individual schools. Ask the relevant DP coordinator rather than assuming one MYP course guarantees or prevents a later subject.


### Common misunderstandings


The IB defines eight subject groups, but it does not require every school to offer multiple courses within each group. Staffing, timetables, enrolment, and national rules influence what is available.


Years 4 and 5 flexibility also does not make every subject optional. Individuals and Societies remains part of the required six-group pattern. MYP requirements should not be confused with DP selection, where students choose distinct subjects such as History, Geography, Economics, or Global Politics. The[overview of all eight MYP subject groups](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/what-subjects-are-taught-in-myp) clarifies this distinction.


### Conclusion


For most students, **MYP Individuals and Societies is compulsory** , including within the permitted six-group model in Years 4 and 5 and for the MYP certificate. What may be optional is the course used to satisfy the requirement.


Check your school handbook and consult the MYP coordinator because local course titles and combinations differ. Once enrolled,[RevisionDojo’s MYP Individuals and Societies resources](https://www.revisiondojo.com/myp/myp-individuals-and-societies) can support criteria-based practice through Study Notes, Flashcards, and the Questionbank when matched to your school’s units.
